adds.title: Brazilian Supreme Federal Court ruling, March 2018 - legal gender change
adds.summary: In March 2018 Brazil's Supreme Federal Court ruled that transgender people may change their legal name and gender marker on civil records without sex-reassignment surgery, hormonal treatment, or judicial authorization.

adds.title: Manaus municipal law banning unisex restrooms - 18 October 2022
adds.summary: On 18 October 2022 Manaus sanctioned a municipal law prohibiting multigender/unisex restrooms.

adds.title: Federal Public Prosecutor's Office (MPF) Recommendation - August 2024
adds.summary: In August 2024, the Federal Public Prosecutor's Office recommended that the state of Amazonas guarantee integral health care to the LGBTQIAPN+ population, including trans people.

adds.title: Amazonas Public Defender's Office (DPE-AM) monitoring process - November 2023
adds.summary: In Amazonas as of 1 November 2023 the State Public Defender's health unit opened a collective procedure to audit SUS care for trans people covering access to hormonization, outpatient services, and lack of accreditation for gender-affirming surgeries including sexual reassignment, and in October 2023 the Manaus Municipal Health Secretariat committed to dispense standardized medications to trans people on prescription from the Codajás Outpatient Clinic that handles hormonization and to designate reference UBS primary-care units in each city zone, while the State Health Secretariat was ordered to report on equitable integral care including remedying hormoniotherapy gaps guaranteed under Federal Council of Medicine Resolution No. 2,265 of 2019.

adds.title: Amazonas State Law No. 6,463/2023 - gender-neutral language ban in schools
adds.summary: On 10 October 2023 Amazonas State Law No. 6,463 expressly prohibited use of neutral language, non-binary dialect, or any expression departing from standard Portuguese in curricula and teaching materials of public and private educational institutions and in official documents of schools and public agencies statewide.

adds.title: Amazonas State Court of Justice (TJAM) booklet Lar e Direito! / Home is a Right! - August 2024
adds.summary: In Amazonas as of August 2024, LGBTQIAPN+ adolescents facing family discrimination and expulsion are guaranteed under ECA Article 17 physical, psychological and moral integrity including identity and autonomy and under Constitution/ECA duties of family, society and State to ensure health, food, education and protection from negligence and discrimination with equal treatment of children regardless of sexual orientation, with bullying criminalized under Law 14.811/2024 by fine to 4 years' imprisonment, homophobia criminalized per 2019 STF ruling as imprescriptible and non-bailable, conversion/"gay cure" therapy prohibited as illegal and ineffective, and legal support available through the Defensoria Especializada em Direitos Humanos.
